questions.prompt: Which of the following aqueous solutions should have the highest boiling point?
questions.explanation:
Boiling point elevation is a colligative property and depends on the number of solute particles in the solution. We need to consider the Van't Hoff factor ($i$) for each solution.
For $\text{NaOH}$, $i \approx 2$ ($\text{Na}^+$, $\text{OH}^-$).
For $\text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4$, $i \approx 3$ ($2\text{Na}^+$, $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$).
For $\text{NH}_4\text{NO}_3$, $i \approx 2$ ($\text{NH}_4^+$, $\text{NO}_3^-$).
For $\text{KNO}_3$, $i \approx 2$ ($\text{K}^+$, $\text{NO}_3^-$).
Since $\text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4$ dissociates into the most particles per mole, it will have the highest boiling point.

questions.prompt: The unit of ebullioscopic constant is
questions.explanation: The ebullioscopic constant ($K_b$) is defined by the formula $\Delta T_b = K_b \cdot m$, where $\Delta T_b$ is the boiling point elevation in Kelvin (K) and $m$ is the molality in $\text{mol kg}^{-1}$. Therefore, the unit of $K_b$ must be $\text{K / (mol kg}^{-1}) = \text{K kg mol}^{-1}$, or $\text{K (molality)}^{-1}$.

questions.prompt: The values of Van't Hoff factors for $\text{KCl}$, $\text{NaCl}$ and $\text{K}_2\text{SO}_4$ respectively, are
questions.explanation:
The Van't Hoff factor ($i$) represents the number of particles a solute dissociates into in a solution.
For $\text{KCl}$: $\text{KCl} \rightarrow \text{K}^+ + \text{Cl}^-$, so $i = 2$.
For $\text{NaCl}$: $\text{NaCl} \rightarrow \text{Na}^+ + \text{Cl}^-$, so $i = 2$.
For $\text{K}_2\text{SO}_4$: $\text{K}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow 2\text{K}^+ + \text{SO}_4^{2-}$, so $i = 3$.
Therefore, the values are $2, 2, \text{ and } 3$ respectively.
